Traumatic events tend to include situations where someone feels extreme fear or helplessness during the situation. Therefore, traumatic events typically involve situations where death or serious injury occurred or could have happened. Examples of traumatic events include violence, physical abuse, sexual abuse, serious motor vehicle accidents, or natural disasters like hurricanes, fires or earthquakes where people are seriously injured or killed. Immediately after a traumatic event, shock and denial are typical responses that people can have. Other reactions include unpredictable emotions, sadness, anger, flashbacks, relationship problems, and even physical symptoms like headaches or nausea. While these feelings are normal, especially within the first few weeks after experiencing a traumatic event, they can also become problematic if they don't improve over time.
